title: How Worried Should You Be About Microplastics?

mock_data.title: How Worried Should You Be About Microplastics?
mock_data.passage:
Let's start off with a fact: you do not, no matter what you've heard, eat a credit card's worth of microplastics each week. At least, not in the course of a normal human diet. But this popular claim has raised alarm, especially as it has been followed by a flurry of studies that have found microplastics accumulating everywhere – even on the highest mountains, in the deepest ocean trenches and in the most remote polar regions – as well as in human heart tissue, livers, kidneys, breast milk and the bloodstream. If they are all over the place, and we can show in some scientific studies that they can lead to some sort of harm, that's cause for major concern, right? Well, no, not necessarily.

The reason microplastics are effectively everywhere is that plastic is truly a marvel. The advent of the first plastic, Bakelite, in the early 20th century ushered in an age of materials manufactured on demand instead of being harvested from nature. As plastics became thinner and cheaper, they spread far and wide, revolutionising food packaging, electronics and medical devices, to name just a few things. But their durability has a downside. Tiny particles have been shedding into the environment for more than a century, and they last a long time, which is why they've been found in the body tissues and bloodstream of animals up and down the food chain – including us – and in many things we consume, such as salt, beer and drinking water.

So yes, microplastics are probably in you. But don't fret just yet. When we think about any kind of pollutant in the body, we need to consider several things. Firstly, there is the question of size, and for microplastics, there is a huge range. Then there's what dosage would show any effect. And finally, whether that effect is actually harmful. As many of the studies involve animals, we also need to ask whether those animal studies can reasonably apply to the average human.

The credit card claim

For microplastics, many of the most worrisome headlines in the news in the past few years have been vague about the size of the microplastics in question, or have relied on studies using outlandishly large doses which are unlikely to reflect day-to-day reality.

The big claim that went viral, and has seemingly stuck around, was that on average every person on the planet is ingesting as much as 5 grams of microplastics per week – or the equivalent of a credit card's worth. It came from a 2019 study that used some really shoddy maths, and it's simply not true unless you're taking a very unusual approach to curbing your spending.

The study in question was financed by the World Wildlife Fund in partnership with the University of Newcastle. It was a review combining the findings of 59 previous studies on microplastics found in food and water. The problem is that some of the studies only measured the number of microplastic particles in a sample and others measured the mass of microplastics. This meant that the researchers had to rely on estimation in order to compare the two types of study. For example, they estimated the mass of microplastic particles found in drinking water using measurements from ocean water and particle counts per litre from drinking water. But microplastics in the ocean and our drinking water aren't necessarily the same – if the average size of a microplastic particle in the ocean is much larger than those in filtered drinking water, the ultimate calculation will be inflated. Subsequent studies looking at the same data found that it was.

So, no, we don't consume 5 grams of microplastics each week – it is likely far, far less. In fact, one study found that most of the world's population ingests just 0.0041 milligrams per week, which is less than a grain of salt. At that rate, it would take you more than 1.2 million weeks, or more than 23,000 years, to plough through a credit card's worth of plastic. If you're immortal, go ahead and worry.

The same researchers did simulations to predict that on average, each person will accumulate 12.2 milligrams of microplastics over the course of their life, but that only 41 nanograms will actually be absorbed by the body.

Fresh concerns have also been raised in the past few weeks over the quality of studies looking at the amount of microplastics in the body. For instance, some studies vaporise tissue samples and then analyse the fumes for the presence of microplastics. However, when fat is vaporised it can produce similar molecules, creating a false positive.

What do microplastics do in the body?

But all of that only addresses the amount of microplastics we consume. What they are doing to us is another question, and one we don't have really solid answers for yet. Some evidence points to behavioural changes and inflammation in mice exposed to microplastics. But the highest dose given to those mice was 1 gram per day, which is astronomical for a human body, let alone a mouse. A study in pigs used 1 gram per week, and found that microplastics exposure affected the expression of 86 genes and induced oxidative stress in the pancreas, which is caused when there aren't enough antioxidants in the body to get rid of unstable molecules that lead to cell damage. But again, the dosage is unrealistic. In fact, in 2022 the World Health Organization warned in a report that most animal studies use concentrations of microplastics much higher than people are typically exposed to, or use larger microplastic particles than are likely to be taken up by the human body. The report also notes that microplastics circulate through our organs differently than they do in rodents, making it difficult to translate findings to humans.

Preliminary studies in humans do exist, and one recent study found that microplastics can accumulate in plaques along with fats, cholesterol and blood cells. In people who had these plastic-infused plaques, researchers saw a higher rate of heart attack and stroke – but we can only say these were correlated, and not that the microplastics themselves caused these outcomes.

Understanding what microplastics are doing to our bodies is complex. Yes, they contain chemicals that could disrupt our body processes, but when assessing the risk, we can't assume that 100 per cent of those chemicals leach into our bodies instantaneously. Research has shown that when we assume an average amount of leaching in our gut, for example, it results in negligible increases in chemical concentration in the surrounding tissue. And these chemicals don't necessarily increase over your lifetime, because they can also leach out of your tissues and exit through your faeces.

Concerns have been raised that other toxins attached to microplastics could be brought into the body. Or they could interfere with immune responses, or cause cell damage or inflammation. But do they cause these effects more than, say, other kinds of air pollution, sun exposure, eating excess sugar or getting a cold? We simply don't know.

It is understandable to think that microplastics could possibly be dangerous to our health, and we should find out whether they really are. It is a claim that feeds into our doomerism feelings about the pollution happening all around us. And just because we don't consume a credit card's worth of plastic every week doesn't mean the underlying concerns aren't valid. But the field is still young, and we don't yet have rigorous data on the effects of microplastics in the body. So I would spend my time worrying about other things until we have more solid research on the effects of microplastics.

In the meantime, we can all do our part to recycle properly and reduce our use of single-use plastics. This will help to keep our environment and our bodies healthier.

Finally, it's good to stay informed but also to be skeptical of sensational headlines. Look for information from reliable sources like scientific organizations and health agencies. This will help you make informed decisions about your health and the environment.

The introduction of Bakelite, the first synthetic plastic, in the early 20th century, inaugurated an era of on-demand materials, circumventing the need for natural resource extraction. When evaluating any potential pollutant within the body, several factors warrant meticulous consideration. Firstly, particle size is a critical determinant, and microplastics exhibit a considerable range in this regard. Secondly, the threshold dosage required to elicit any discernible effect must be ascertained. And finally, the nature of that effect – specifically, whether it is genuinely deleterious – must be established. Furthermore, given that numerous studies rely on animal models, the applicability of these findings to the average human warrants careful scrutiny.

Unless one is engaging in highly unorthodox dietary practices, this assertion is patently false. The study in question, commissioned by the World Wildlife Fund in collaboration with the University of Newcastle, was a meta-analysis synthesizing findings from 59 prior studies examining microplastics in food and water. A fundamental flaw lay in the inconsistent reporting metrics across these studies, with some quantifying microplastic particles by count and others by mass. This necessitated reliance on estimations to facilitate comparative analysis. For instance, the researchers extrapolated the mass of microplastic particles in drinking water based on measurements from ocean water and particle counts per liter in drinking water. If the average size of a microplastic particle in the ocean substantially exceeds that of those in filtered drinking water, the resulting calculation will be artificially inflated. Consequently, the assertion of consuming 5 grams of microplastics weekly is demonstrably inaccurate; the actual figure is likely far lower. Indeed, one study estimated the average global intake to be a mere 0.0041 milligrams per week, less than a grain of salt. At this rate, it would require over 1.2 million weeks, or more than 23,000 years, to ingest a credit card's worth of plastic. For example, some studies employ tissue vaporization followed by analysis of the resulting fumes for microplastic presence. However, the vaporization of fat can generate molecules mimicking microplastics, leading to false positive results.

While the preceding discussion addresses the quantity of microplastics ingested, their biological impact remains a separate and largely unanswered question. Some evidence suggests behavioral alterations and inflammation in mice exposed to microplastics. However, the highest dose administered to these mice was 1 gram per day – an astronomically high amount relative to human physiology, let alone that of a mouse. A study involving pigs, utilizing a weekly dose of 1 gram, found that microplastic exposure altered the expression of 86 genes and induced oxidative stress in the pancreas, a condition arising from insufficient antioxidant capacity to neutralize unstable molecules that cause cellular damage. Yet again, the dosage is unrealistically high. Indeed, in 2022, the World Health Organization issued a report cautioning that most animal studies employ microplastic concentrations far exceeding typical human exposure levels or utilize larger microplastic particles than are likely to be absorbed by the human body. The report further noted disparities in microplastic circulation patterns between human and rodent organ systems, complicating the extrapolation of findings to humans.

Individuals with these plastic-laden plaques exhibited a higher incidence of heart attack and stroke; however, this observation only establishes a correlation, not a causal relationship, between microplastics and these adverse outcomes.

While they contain chemicals with the potential to disrupt physiological processes, risk assessment cannot assume instantaneous and complete leaching of these chemicals into the body. Research indicates that assuming an average leaching rate within the gut, for instance, results in negligible increases in chemical concentration within surrounding tissues. Furthermore, these chemical levels do not necessarily escalate over one's lifetime, as they can also leach out of tissues and be excreted via feces.

However, whether these effects are more pronounced than those elicited by other environmental stressors, such as air pollution, sun exposure, excessive sugar consumption, or viral infections, remains unknown.

The apprehension surrounding the potential health risks posed by microplastics is understandable, and further investigation is warranted. Such concerns resonate with prevailing anxieties regarding pervasive environmental pollution. And while the claim of ingesting a credit card's worth of plastic weekly may be unfounded, the underlying concerns regarding microplastic exposure remain valid. However, the field of microplastic research is still in its nascent stages, and robust data regarding their effects on the human body are currently lacking. Therefore, focusing one's anxieties on other, better-understood health risks would be a more prudent course of action pending the availability of more definitive research on the effects of microplastics. Until then, it would be wise to exercise a degree of circumspection.

mock_data.translation:
Keling, bir faktdan boshlaylik: siz, nima eshitgan bo'lsangiz ham, har hafta kredit karta miqdoridagi mikroplastikni yemaysiz. Hech bo'lmaganda, oddiy inson ovqatlanishi davomida emas. Ammo bu mashhur da'vo tashvish uyg'otdi, ayniqsa mikroplastiklar hamma joyda – eng baland tog'larda, eng chuqur okean xandaqlarida va eng uzoq qutb hududlarida – shuningdek, inson yurak to'qimasi, jigar, buyrak, ko'krak suti va qon tarkibida topilganligini ko'rsatgan tadqiqotlar to'lqini bilan. Agar ular hamma joyda bo'lsa va ba'zi ilmiy tadqiqotlarda ular biron bir zararga olib kelishi mumkinligini ko'rsata olsak, bu jiddiy tashvish uchun sabab, to'g'rimi? Xo'sh, yo'q, shart emas.

Mikroplastikalarning hamma joyda bo'lishining sababi shundaki, plastik haqiqatan ham mo'jiza. 20-asrning boshlarida birinchi plastik Bakelit paydo bo'lishi tabiatdan yig'ish o'rniga talab bo'yicha ishlab chiqariladigan materiallar davrini boshladi. Plastiklar yupqalashib va arzonlashgan sari ular keng tarqaldi, oziq-ovqat qadoqlash, elektronika va tibbiy asboblarni inqilob qildi, faqat bir nechtasini aytish uchun. Ammo ularning chidamliligi salbiy tomonga ega. Mayda zarrachalar bir asrdan ko'proq vaqtdan beri atrof-muhitga to'kilmoqda va ular uzoq vaqt davom etadi, shuning uchun ular oziq-ovqat zanjiri bo'ylab hayvonlarning tana to'qimalari va qon tarkibida topilgan – shu jumladan bizda – va biz iste'mol qiladigan ko'p narsalarda, masalan, tuz, pivo va ichimlik suvida.

Ha, mikroplastiklar sizda bo'lishi mumkin. Lekin hali tashvislanmang. Tanadagi har qanday ifloslantiruvchi haqida o'ylaganimizda, bir nechta narsani hisobga olishimiz kerak. Birinchidan, o'lcham masalasi bor, va mikroplastiklar uchun juda katta diapazon mavjud. Keyin qanday dozada biron bir ta'sir ko'rsatishi masalasi bor. Va nihoyat, bu ta'sir haqiqatan ham zararli yoki yo'qligi. Ko'pgina tadqiqotlar hayvonlarni o'z ichiga olganligi sababli, biz hayvonlar ustida o'tkazilgan tadqiqotlar o'rtacha insonga tegishli bo'lishi mumkinmi deb so'rashimiz kerak.

Kredit karta da'vosi

Mikroplastiklar uchun so'nggi bir necha yildagi eng tashvishli sarlavhalarning ko'pchiligi ko'rib chiqilayotgan mikroplastiklarning o'lchami haqida noaniq bo'lgan yoki kundalik hayotni aks ettirishi dargumon bo'lgan juda katta dozalardan foydalanadigan tadqiqotlarga tayanган.

Viral bo'lgan va atrofda qolgan katta da'vo shunday ediki, o'rtacha sayyoradagi har bir odam har hafta 5 grammgacha mikroplastikni yutmoqda – yoki kredit karta miqdoriga teng. Bu juda sifatsiz matematikadan foydalangan 2019 yilgi tadqiqotdan kelib chiqqan va agar siz xarajatlaringizni qisqartirishning juda g'ayrioddiy usulini qo'llamasangiz, bu shunchaki to'g'ri emas.

Ushbu tadqiqot Jahon yovvoyi tabiat fondi tomonidan Nyukasl universiteti bilan hamkorlikda moliyalashtirilgan. Bu oziq-ovqat va suvda topilgan mikroplastiklar bo'yicha 59 ta oldingi tadqiqot natijalarini birlashtirgan tahlil edi. Muammo shundaki, ba'zi tadqiqotlar namunadagi mikroplastik zarralar sonini o'lchagan va boshqalari mikroplastiklarning massasini o'lchagan. Bu esa tadqiqotchilar ikki turdagi tadqiqotni solishtirish uchun taxminga tayanishi kerak bo'lganini anglatardi. Masalan, ular ichimlik suvida topilgan mikroplastik zarralarning massasini okean suvidagi o'lchovlar va ichimlik suvidagi litr boshiga zarracha soni yordamida taxmin qildilar. Ammo okeandagi va bizning ichimlik suvimizdagi mikroplastiklar bir xil bo'lishi shart emas – agar okeandagi mikroplastik zarraning o'rtacha o'lchami filtrlangan ichimlik suvidagilardan ancha katta bo'lsa, yakuniy hisoblash shishirilgan bo'ladi. Keyingi tadqiqotlar xuddi shu ma'lumotlarga qarab, shunday ekanligini aniqladilar.

Demak, yo'q, biz har hafta 5 gramm mikroplastik iste'mol qilmaymiz – bu ancha, ancha kam bo'lishi ehtimoli bor. Aslida, bitta tadqiqot dunyo aholisining aksariyati har hafta atigi 0,0041 milligramm yutishini aniqladi, bu tuz donasidan ham kam. Shu tezlikda kredit karta miqdoridagi plastikni iste'mol qilish uchun sizga 1,2 million haftadan ko'proq yoki 23 000 yildan ko'proq vaqt kerak bo'ladi. Agar siz abadiy yashasangiz, davom eting va tashvishlanig.

Xuddi shu tadqiqotchilar simulyatsiyalar o'tkazib, o'rtacha har bir odam umri davomida 12,2 milligramm mikroplastik to'plashini, lekin faqat 41 nanogramm aslida tana tomonidan so'rilishini bashorat qildilar.

So'nggi bir necha haftada tanadagi mikroplastiklar miqdorini o'rganadigan tadqiqotlar sifati ustidan ham yangi tashvishlar paydo bo'ldi. Masalan, ba'zi tadqiqotlar to'qima namunalarini bug'latadi va keyin mikroplastiklar mavjudligi uchun tutunni tahlil qiladi. Biroq, yog' bug'latirilganda u o'xshash molekulalar hosil qilishi mumkin, bu noto'g'ri ijobiy natija yaratadi.

Mikroplastiklar tanada nima qiladi?

Ammo bularning barchasi faqat biz iste'mol qiladigan mikroplastiklar miqdorini ko'rib chiqadi. Ular bizga nima qilayotgani boshqa savol va biz hali aniq javobga ega emasmiz. Ba'zi dalillar mikroplastiklarga duchor bo'lgan sichqonlarda xulq-atvor o'zgarishlari va yallig'lanishni ko'rsatadi. Ammo o'sha sichqonlarga berilgan eng yuqori doza kuniga 1 gramm edi, bu inson tanasi uchun astronomik, sichqoncha haqida gapirmasa ham. Cho'chqalardagi tadqiqot haftasiga 1 gramm ishlatdi va mikroplastiklar ta'siri 86 genning ifodalanishiga ta'sir qilganini va oshqozon osti bezida oksidlovchi stressni keltirib chiqarganini aniqladi, bu tanada hujayralar shikastlanishiga olib keladigan beqaror molekulalarni yo'q qilish uchun yetarli antioksidantlar bo'lmaganda sodir bo'ladi. Ammo yana, dozaj real emas. Aslida, 2022-yilda Jahon sog'liqni saqlash tashkiloti hisobotida ko'pgani hayvonlar tadqiqotlari odamlar odatda duchor bo'ladigan mikroplastiklar konsentratsiyasidan ancha yuqori konsentratsiya ishlatishini yoki inson tanasi tomonidan qabul qilinishi ehtimoli bo'lgan mikroplastik zarralardan kattaroq zarralar ishlatishini ogohlantirdi. Hisobotda, shuningdek, mikroplastiklar bizning a'zolarimiz orqali kemiruvchilardagidan farqli ravishda aylanishi qayd etilgan, bu topilmalarni insonga tarjima qilishni qiyinlashtiradi.

Insonlardagi dastlabki tadqiqotlar mavjud va yaqinda o'tkazilgan bitta tadqiqot mikroplastiklar yog'lar, xolesterin va qon hujayralari bilan birga plyaklarda to'planishi mumkinligini aniqladi. Plastik bilan to'yingan plyaklarga ega odamlarda tadqiqotchilar yurak xurujlari va insultning yuqoriroq darajasini ko'rdilar – lekin biz faqat bular o'zaro bog'liq ekanligini ayta olamiz, mikroplastiklarning o'zi bu natijalarga sabab bo'lganini emas.

Mikroplastiklar tanalarimizga nima qilayotganini tushunish murakkab. Ha, ular tana jarayonlarini buzishi mumkin bo'lgan kimyoviy moddalarni o'z ichiga oladi, lekin xavfni baholashda biz bu kimyoviy moddalarning 100 foizi bir zumda tanalarimizga singib ketadi deb taxmin qila olmaymiz. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, masalan, ichagimizda o'rtacha miqdorda singish deb faraz qilsak, bu atrofdagi to'qimadagi kimyoviy konsentratsiyaning ahamiyatsiz o'sishiga olib keladi. Va bu kimyoviy moddalar umr davomida ortib borishi shart emas, chunki ular to'qimalaringizdan singib chiqishi va axlat orqali chiqishi mumkin.

Mikroplastiklarga biriktirilgan boshqa toksinlar tanaga kiritilishi mumkinligi haqida tashvishlar bildirilgan. Yoki ular immun javoblariga xalaqit berishi, hujayra shikastlanishi yoki yallig'lanishga sabab bo'lishi mumkin. Ammo ular bu ta'sirlarni, aytaylik, boshqa turdagi havo ifloslanishi, quyosh ta'siri, ortiqcha shakar iste'mol qilish yoki shamollashdan ko'proq keltirib chiqaradimi? Biz shunchaki bilmaymiz.

Mikroplastiklar bizning sog'lig'imiz uchun xavfli bo'lishi mumkin deb o'ylash tushunarli va biz ularning haqiqatan ham shunday ekanligini aniqlashimiz kerak. Bu atrofimizda sodir bo'layotgan ifloslanish haqidagi pessimizm hislarimizni oziqlantiruvchi da'vo. Va biz har hafta kredit karta miqdoridagi plastik iste'mol qilmasligimiz asosiy tashvishlar ahamiyatsiz degani emas. Ammo soha hali yosh va biz tanadagi mikroplastiklar ta'siri haqida hali qat'iy ma'lumotlarga ega emasmiz. Shuning uchun men mikroplastiklar ta'siri bo'yicha mustahkamroq tadqiqotlar bo'lgunga qadar boshqa narsalar haqida tashvishlanishga vaqt sarflardim.

Bundan tashqari, ularning inson to'qimalarida, jumladan, yurak, jigar, buyraklar, ona suti va qon oqimida aniqlanishi bu xavotirlarni yanada kuchaytirdi. Ularning hamma joyda mavjudligi va ayrim tadqiqotlar bilan ko'rsatilgan zarar yetkazish potentsiali nuqtai nazaridan, xavotirlanishga jiddiy sabab borligi o'z-o'zidan ravshan ko'rinadi, shunday emasmi? Biroq, bunday xulosaga kelish shart emas.

Mikroplastmassalarning hamma joyda mavjudligi, plastmassalarni juda zarur qilgan xususiyatlardan kelib chiqadi. 20-asrning boshlarida birinchi sintetik plastmassa bo'lgan Bakelitning joriy etilishi, tabiiy resurslarni qazib olish zaruratini chetlab o'tadigan, talabga binoan materiallar davrini boshlab berdi. Plastmassalar tobora arzon va ko'p qirrali bo'lib borgan sari, ularning ko'payishi oziq-ovqat mahsulotlarini qadoqlash va elektronikadan tortib tibbiy asboblargacha bo'lgan sohalarda inqilob qildi. Biroq, ularning foydaliligini ta'minlaydigan chidamlilik ularning "Axilles to'pig'i" hamdir. Bir asrdan ortiq vaqt davomida bu materiallar atrof-muhitga mayda zarralarni chiqarib kelmoqda va ularning tabiiy barqarorligi ularning uzoq umrini ta'minlaydi, shu bilan ularning oziq-ovqat zanjiri bo'ylab organizmlarning to'qimalari va qon aylanish tizimlarida, shu jumladan odamlarda, shuningdek, tuz, pivo va ichimlik suvi kabi keng iste'mol qilinadigan mahsulotlarda aniqlanishini tushuntiradi.

Shunday qilib, mikroplastmassalarning sizning tizimingizda mavjud bo'lish ehtimoli katta. Biroq, muddatidan oldin xavotirlanishga hojat yo'q. Tanadagi har qanday potentsial ifloslantiruvchi moddani baholashda bir nechta omillarni diqqat bilan ko'rib chiqish kerak. Birinchidan, zarracha hajmi muhim determinant hisoblanadi va mikroplastmassalar bu borada sezilarli diapazonga ega. Ikkinchidan, har qanday sezilarli ta'sirni keltirib chiqarish uchun zarur bo'lgan chegara dozasi aniqlanishi kerak. Va nihoyat, bu ta'sirning tabiati - xususan, u haqiqatan ham zararli ekanligi - aniqlanishi kerak. Bundan tashqari, ko'plab tadqiqotlar hayvonlar modellariga asoslanganligini hisobga olsak, bu natijalarning o'rtacha odamga qo'llanilishi diqqat bilan o'rganishni talab qiladi.

Mikroplastmassalarga kelsak, so'nggi yillarda yangiliklar tsiklida tarqalgan ko'plab shov-shuvli sarlavhalar yoki tekshirilayotgan mikroplastmassalarning hajmi bo'yicha ataylab noaniq bo'lgan, yoki real dunyo ta'sir qilish stsenariylariga umuman o'xshamaydigan, noreal yuqori dozalarni qo'llagan tadqiqotlarga asoslangan.

Yuqorida aytib o'tilgan virusli da'vo, har bir kishi uchun o'rtacha haftalik 5 gramm mikroplastmassa yutish - kredit kartaga teng - metodologik kamchiliklar va soxta hisob-kitoblar bilan buzilgan 2019-yilgi tadqiqotdan kelib chiqqan. Agar kimdir g'ayrioddiy ovqatlanish amaliyotlari bilan shug'ullanmasa, bu da'vo mutlaqo noto'g'ri. Jahon yovvoyi tabiat fondi tomonidan Nyukasl universiteti bilan hamkorlikda buyurtma qilingan tadqiqot, oziq-ovqat va suvdagi mikroplastmassalarni tekshirgan 59 ta oldingi tadqiqot natijalarini sintez qilgan meta-tahlil edi. Asosiy kamchilik bu tadqiqotlar bo'yicha nomuvofiq hisobot ko'rsatkichlarida yotardi, ba'zilari mikroplastmassa zarralarini hisob bo'yicha, boshqalari esa massa bo'yicha miqdoriy baholagan. Bu qiyosiy tahlilni osonlashtirish uchun baholashga tayanishni zarur qildi. Misol uchun, tadqiqotchilar ichimlik suvidagi mikroplastmassa zarralarining massasini okean suvidagi o'lchovlar va ichimlik suvidagi litr uchun zarracha soniga asoslanib ekstrapolyatsiya qilishdi. Biroq, okeandagi mikroplastmassalar ichimlik suvidagilar bilan bir xil, degan taxmin namoyish etilganidek noto'g'ri. Agar okeanda mikroplastmassa zarrasining o'rtacha hajmi filtrlangan ichimlik suvidagilardan sezilarli darajada oshsa, natijada olingan hisob-kitob sun'iy ravishda oshiriladi. Xuddi shu ma'lumotlar to'plamidan foydalangan holda keyingi tekshiruvlar bu da'voni tasdiqladi.

Natijada, haftasiga 5 gramm mikroplastmassa iste'mol qilish da'vosi namoyish etilganidek noto'g'ri; haqiqiy raqam ancha past bo'lishi mumkin. Darhaqiqat, bir tadqiqotda global o'rtacha iste'mol haftasiga atigi 0,0041 milligramm, bir chimdim tuzdan ham kamroq, deb baholangan. Bu darajada, kredit karta qiymatiga teng plastmassani yutish uchun 1,2 million haftadan ko'proq yoki 23 000 yildan ko'proq vaqt kerak bo'ladi. Faqatgina cheksiz umrga ega bo'lganlar bu istiqbolga xavotirlanishlari kerak.

Xuddi shu tadqiqotchilar simulyatsiyalardan foydalanib, har bir kishi uchun o'rtacha umr bo'yi 12,2 milligramm mikroplastmassa to'planishini prognoz qilishdi, shundan atigi 41 nanogramm haqiqatda tanaga so'riladi.

Bundan tashqari, yaqinda tanadagi mikroplastmassalarni miqdoriy baholash tadqiqotlarining metodologik qat'iyligi borasida xavotirlar paydo bo'ldi. Misol uchun, ba'zi tadqiqotlar to'qimalarni bug'lantirishdan so'ng, mikroplastmassalarning mavjudligi uchun hosil bo'lgan tutunni tahlil qilishdan foydalanadi. Biroq, yog'ni bug'lantirish mikroplastmassalarga taqlid qiladigan molekulalarni hosil qilishi mumkin, bu esa noto'g'ri ijobiy natijalarga olib keladi.

Yuqoridagi munozara yutilgan mikroplastmassalar miqdoriga qaratilgan bo'lsa-da, ularning biologik ta'siri alohida va asosan javobsiz qolgan savol bo'lib qolmoqda. Ba'zi dalillar mikroplastmassalarga ta'sir qilgan sichqonlarda xulq-atvor o'zgarishlari va yallig'lanishni ko'rsatadi. Biroq, bu sichqonlarga berilgan eng yuqori doza kuniga 1 gramm edi - inson fiziologiyasiga nisbatan astronomik darajada yuqori miqdor, sichqonnikini aytmasa ham bo'ladi. Haftasiga 1 gramm doza ishlatgan cho'chqalar ishtirokidagi tadqiqotda mikroplastmassalarga ta'sir qilish 86 ta genni ifodalashni o'zgartirganligi va oshqozon osti bezida oksidlovchi stressni keltirib chiqarganligi aniqlandi, bu hujayralarga zarar yetkazadigan beqaror molekulalarni zararsizlantirish uchun etarli antioksidant qobiliyatining yo'qligidan kelib chiqadigan holatdir. Yana, doza noreal darajada yuqori. Darhaqiqat, 2022-yilda Jahon sog'liqni saqlash tashkiloti hayvonlar ustida o'tkazilgan ko'pchilik tadqiqotlarda mikroplastmassa konsentratsiyasi inson ta'sirining odatdagi darajasidan ancha yuqori yoki inson tanasi tomonidan so'rilishi mumkin bo'lganidan kattaroq mikroplastmassa zarralaridan foydalaniladi, degan ogohlantirish bilan hisobot chiqardi. Hisobotda, shuningdek, inson va kemiruvchilar organ tizimlari o'rtasidagi mikroplastmassa aylanish naqshlaridagi nomuvofiqliklar natijalarni odamlarga ekstrapolyatsiya qilishni qiyinlashtirishi qayd etilgan.

Inson ustida o'tkazilgan dastlabki tadqiqotlar mavjud, yaqinda o'tkazilgan bir tadqiqotda mikroplastmassalarning yog'lar, xolesterin va qon hujayralari bilan birga blyashkalar ichida to'planishi aniqlangan. Ushbu plastmassa bilan to'ldirilgan blyashkalarga ega bo'lgan shaxslarda yurak xuruji va insult holatlari ko'proq uchragan; biroq, bu kuzatuv faqat mikroplastmassalar va ushbu salbiy oqibatlar o'rtasida sababiy bog'liqlikni emas, balki korrelyatsiyani o'rnatadi.

Mikroplastmassalarning inson salomatligiga aniq ta'sirini aniqlash murakkab ishdir. Ular fiziologik jarayonlarni buzish potentsialiga ega bo'lgan kimyoviy moddalarni o'z ichiga olgan bo'lsa-da, xavfni baholash ushbu kimyoviy moddalarning tanaga bir zumda va to'liq sizib chiqishini taxmin qila olmaydi. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, masalan, ichakdagi o'rtacha sizib chiqish tezligini taxmin qilish, atrofdagi to'qimalarda kimyoviy moddalar konsentratsiyasining ahamiyatsiz darajada oshishiga olib keladi. Bundan tashqari, bu kimyoviy moddalar darajasi bir umr davomida doimiy ravishda oshmaydi, chunki ular to'qimalardan ham sizib chiqishi va najas orqali chiqarilishi mumkin.

Mikroplastmassalarning boshqa toksinlarni tanaga tashish, immunitet javoblariga xalaqit berish yoki hujayralarga zarar yetkazish va yallig'lanishni keltirib chiqarish potentsiali borasida xavotirlar bildirilgan. Biroq, bu ta'sirlar havo ifloslanishi, quyosh ta'siri, ortiqcha shakar iste'mol qilish yoki virusli infektsiyalar kabi boshqa atrof-muhit stresslari ta'siridan ko'ra ko'proq aniqmi yoki yo'qmi, noma'lumligicha qolmoqda.

Mikroplastmassalar keltirib chiqarishi mumkin bo'lgan salomatlik xavflari bilan bog'liq xavotir tushunarli va qo'shimcha tekshiruv o'tkazish kerak. Bunday xavotirlar atrof-muhitning keng tarqalgan ifloslanishi bilan bog'liq bo'lgan dolzarb xavotirlarga mos keladi. Va haftasiga kredit karta qiymatiga teng plastmassa yutish da'vosi asossiz bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, mikroplastmassalarga ta'sir qilish bilan bog'liq asosiy xavotirlar o'z kuchida qolmoqda. Biroq, mikroplastmassa tadqiqotlari sohasi hali endigina rivojlanayotgan bosqichda va ularning inson tanasiga ta'siri haqida ishonchli ma'lumotlar hozirda yetishmaydi. Shuning uchun, mikroplastmassalarning ta'siri bo'yicha yanada aniqroq tadqiqotlar mavjud bo'lgunga qadar, o'z xavotirlaringizni boshqa, yaxshiroq tushunilgan salomatlik xavflariga qaratish oqilona harakat bo'ladi. Ungacha muayyan darajada ehtiyotkorlikni saqlash oqilona bo'ladi.
